sanskrit: ato 'nyathā vartamānāḥ sarve nārhanti satkriyām tasmān nityaṃ parīkṣeta puruṣān praṇidhāya vai
english: Those who conduct themselves otherwise than this are none of them worthy of honor; therefore one should ever examine men, observing them closely with care.

sanskrit: akrodhaḥ satyavacanam ahiṃsā dama ārjavam adroho nātimānaś ca hrīs titikṣā tapaḥ śamaḥ
english: Freedom from anger, truthful speech, non-injury, self-restraint, uprightness, freedom from malice, absence of pride, modesty, forbearance, austerity, tranquillity—

sanskrit: yasminn etāni dṛśyante na cākāryāṇi bhārata bhāvato viniviṣṭāni tat pātraṃ mānam arhati
english: the man in whom these are seen, firmly settled by their very nature, O Bhārata, and who does no forbidden deeds—that one is a worthy vessel, deserving of honor.

sanskrit: tathā ciroṣitaṃ cāpi saṃpratyāgatam eva ca apūrvaṃ caiva pūrvaṃ ca tat pātraṃ mānam arhati
english: So too one long abiding here, or one but newly arrived, whether a stranger never seen before or an old acquaintance—such a vessel deserves honor.

sanskrit: aprāmāṇyaṃ ca vedānāṃ śāstrāṇāṃ cātilaṅghanam sarvatra cānavasthānam etan nāśanam ātmanaḥ
english: To deny the authority of the Vedas, to overstep the sacred treatises, and to lack steadfastness in all things—this is the ruin of one's own self.

sanskrit: bhavet paṇḍitamānī yo brāhmaṇo vedanindakaḥ ānvīkṣikīṃ tarkavidyām anurakto nirarthikām
english: The brāhmaṇa who fancies himself learned, who reviles the Vedas, who is devoted to the science of logic and to fruitless disputation,

sanskrit: hetuvādān bruvan satsu vijetāhetuvādikaḥ ākroṣṭā cātivaktā ca brāhmaṇānāṃ sadaiva hi
english: who utters arguments of mere reasoning amid the good, a refuter who confounds those who do not so reason, and who is forever a reviler and abuser of brāhmaṇas—

sanskrit: sarvābhiśaṅkī mūḍhaś ca bālaḥ kaṭukavāg api boddhavyas tādṛśas tāta naraśvānaṃ hi taṃ viduḥ
english: suspicious of all, deluded, childish, and harsh of tongue—such a one, my son, is to be recognized for what he is, for they call him a dog among men.

sanskrit: yathā śvā bhaṣituṃ caiva hantuṃ caivāvasṛjyate evaṃ saṃbhāṣaṇārthāya sarvaśāstravadhāya ca alpaśrutāḥ kutarkāś ca dṛṣṭāḥ spṛṣṭāḥ kupaṇḍitāḥ
english: As a dog is let loose to bark and to bite, so are such men loosed for wrangling and for the slaughter of all the scriptures; men of little learning, given to crooked logic—such false scholars are seen and met with everywhere.

sanskrit: śrutismṛtītihāsādipurāṇāraṇyavedinaḥ anurundhyād bahujñāṃś ca sārajñāṃś caiva paṇḍitān
english: One should seek out the learned—those versed in śruti, smṛti, the chronicles, the purāṇas, and the forest-treatises, men of wide knowledge who grasp the essence of things.

sanskrit: lokayātrā ca draṣṭavyā dharmaś cātmahitāni ca evaṃ naro vartamānaḥ śāśvatīr edhate samāḥ
english: The course of worldly life must be observed, and dharma, and what is for one's own good; the man who so conducts himself flourishes through everlasting years.

sanskrit: ṛṇam unmucya devānām ṛṣīṇāṃ ca tathaiva ca pitṝṇām atha viprāṇām atithīnāṃ ca pañcamam
english: Having discharged his debt to the gods, and likewise to the seers, to the ancestors, to the brāhmaṇas, and as the fifth, to guests,

sanskrit: paryāyeṇa viśuddhena sunirṇiktena karmaṇā evaṃ gṛhasthaḥ karmāṇi kurvan dharmān na hīyate
english: in due order, with pure and well-cleansed action—thus the householder, performing his works, falls not away from his sacred duties.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca strīṇāṃ svabhāvam icchāmi śrotuṃ bharatasattama striyo hi mūlaṃ doṣāṇāṃ laghucittāḥ pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I wish to hear of the nature of women, O best of the Bhāratas; for women are the root of faults, and light of mind, O grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam nāradasya ca saṃvādaṃ puṃścalyā pañcacūḍayā
english: Bhīṣma said: On this they relate an ancient tale of old—the dialogue between Nārada and the wanton apsaras Pañcacūḍā.

sanskrit: lokān anucaran dhīmān devarṣir nāradaḥ purā dadarśāpsarasaṃ brāhmīṃ pañcacūḍām aninditām
english: Of old, as the wise divine seer Nārada wandered through the worlds, he beheld the blameless apsaras Pañcacūḍā, born of Brahmā.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā cārusarvāṅgīṃ papracchāpsarasaṃ muniḥ saṃśayo hṛdi me kaś cit tan me brūhi sumadhyame
english: Seeing her, lovely in every limb, the sage questioned the apsaras: 'A certain doubt stirs within my heart; tell me of it, O slender-waisted one.'

sanskrit: evam uktā tu sā vipraṃ pratyuvācātha nāradam viṣaye sati vakṣyāmi samarthāṃ manyase ca mām
english: Thus addressed, she answered the brāhmaṇa Nārada: 'If it lie within my province I shall speak of it, and if you deem me equal to the task.'

sanskrit: nārada uvāca na tvām aviṣaye bhadre niyokṣyāmi kathaṃ cana strīṇāṃ svabhāvam icchāmi tvattaḥ śrotuṃ varānane
english: Nārada said: I shall in no way set you, gentle lady, to a matter beyond your province; I wish to hear from you, O fair-faced one, the nature of women.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca etac chrutvā vacas tasya devarṣer apsarottamā pratyuvāca na śakṣyāmi strī satī nindituṃ striyaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Hearing this word of the divine seer, the foremost of apsarases replied: 'I shall not be able, being myself a woman, to censure women.'

sanskrit: viditās te striyo yāś ca yādṛśāś ca svabhāvataḥ na mām arhasi devarṣe niyoktuṃ praśna īdṛśe
english: 'Women are known to you, both who they are and of what nature they are; you ought not, O divine seer, to set me to a question such as this.'

sanskrit: tām uvāca sa devarṣiḥ satyaṃ vada sumadhyame mṛṣāvāde bhaved doṣaḥ satye doṣo na vidyate
english: To her the divine seer said: 'Speak the truth, O slender-waisted one; in false speech there is fault, but in truth no fault is found.'

sanskrit: ity uktā sā kṛtamatir abhavac cāruhāsinī strīdoṣāñ śāśvatān satyān bhāṣituṃ saṃpracakrame
english: Thus addressed, the sweetly smiling one made up her mind, and set herself to declare the everlasting and true faults of women.

sanskrit: pañcacūḍovāca kulīnā rūpavatyaś ca nāthavatyaś ca yoṣitaḥ maryādāsu na tiṣṭhanti sa doṣaḥ strīṣu nārada
english: Pañcacūḍā said: Women of good family, beautiful, and possessed of protectors do not abide within the bounds of propriety; that, Nārada, is the fault in women.

sanskrit: na strībhyaḥ kiṃ cid anyad vai pāpīyastaram asti vai striyo hi mūlaṃ doṣāṇāṃ tathā tvam api vettha ha
english: There is indeed nothing else more given to wickedness than women, for women are the root of faults; this too you yourself well know.

sanskrit: samājñātān ṛddhimataḥ pratirūpān vaśe sthitān patīn antaram āsādya nālaṃ nāryaḥ pratīkṣitum
english: Though their husbands be renowned, prosperous, comely, and wholly devoted, women, finding an opening, are unable to remain faithful.

sanskrit: asaddharmas tv ayaṃ strīṇām asmākaṃ bhavati prabho pāpīyaso narān yad vai lajjāṃ tyaktvā bhajāmahe
english: This is the wicked way of us women, O lord—that, casting off shame, we consort with men more base than our own.

sanskrit: striyaṃ hi yaḥ prārthayate saṃnikarṣaṃ ca gacchati īṣac ca kurute sevāṃ tam evecchanti yoṣitaḥ
english: For whoever woos a woman, draws near to her, and renders her but a little service—him the women desire.

sanskrit: anarthitvān manuṣyāṇāṃ bhayāt parijanasya ca maryādāyām amaryādāḥ striyas tiṣṭhanti bhartṛṣu
english: Only because men do not solicit them, and out of fear of their kinsfolk, do women—unrestrained though they are—abide within bounds and stay with their husbands.

sanskrit: nāsāṃ kaś cid agamyo 'sti nāsāṃ vayasi saṃsthitiḥ virūpaṃ rūpavantaṃ vā pumān ity eva bhuñjate
english: For them no man is forbidden, nor have they any fixed regard for age; be he ugly or handsome, they enjoy him simply because he is a man.

sanskrit: na bhayān nāpy anukrośān nārthahetoḥ kathaṃ cana na jñātikulasaṃbandhāt striyas tiṣṭhanti bhartṛṣu
english: Not from fear, nor from compassion, nor for the sake of wealth in any way, nor from the bond of kindred and family do women remain with their husbands.

sanskrit: yauvane vartamānānāṃ mṛṣṭābharaṇavāsasām nārīṇāṃ svairavṛttānāṃ spṛhayanti kulastriyaḥ
english: Women of good families yearn after those women who, being in the flush of youth, adorned with bright ornaments and raiment, live as they please.

sanskrit: yāś ca śaśvad bahumatā rakṣyante dayitāḥ striyaḥ api tāḥ saṃprasajjante kubjāndhajaḍavāmanaiḥ
english: Even those women who are forever highly esteemed, cherished, and guarded—even they cleave to hunchbacks, the blind, the dull-witted, and dwarfs.

sanskrit: paṅguṣv api ca devarṣe ye cānye kutsitā narāḥ strīṇām agamyo loke 'smin nāsti kaś cin mahāmune
english: Even to the lame, O divine seer, and to other men despised—in this world, O great sage, there is no man forbidden to women.

sanskrit: yadi puṃsāṃ gatir brahma kathaṃ cin nopapadyate apy anyonyaṃ pravartante na hi tiṣṭhanti bhartṛṣu
english: If, O holy one, access to men in no way befalls them, they will resort even to one another, for they cannot abide content with their husbands.

sanskrit: alābhāt puruṣāṇāṃ hi bhayāt parijanasya ca vadhabandhabhayāc cāpi svayaṃ guptā bhavanti tāḥ
english: For want of men, from fear of their household, and from dread of slaying and bondage, they keep themselves guarded of their own accord.

sanskrit: calasvabhāvā duḥsevyā durgrāhyā bhāvatas tathā prājñasya puruṣasyeha yathā vācas tathā striyaḥ
english: Fickle by nature, hard to serve, and by their disposition hard to grasp—women are even as the speech of a wise man here below.

sanskrit: nāgnis tṛpyati kāṣṭhānāṃ nāpagānāṃ mahodadhiḥ nāntakaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ na puṃsāṃ vāmalocanāḥ
english: As fire is never sated with fuel, nor the great ocean with rivers, nor Death with all beings, so are the fair-eyed ones never sated with men.

sanskrit: idam anyac ca devarṣe rahasyaṃ sarvayoṣitām dṛṣṭvaiva puruṣaṃ hṛdyaṃ yoniḥ praklidyate striyaḥ
english: And here is another secret of all womankind, O divine seer: at the mere sight of a pleasing man, a woman's loins grow moist with desire.

sanskrit: kāmānām api dātāraṃ kartāraṃ mānasāntvayoḥ rakṣitāraṃ na mṛṣyanti bhartāraṃ paramaṃ striyaḥ
english: Even a husband who grants their every desire, who shows them honor and tender words, who is their guardian—even such a peerless husband women do not patiently endure.

sanskrit: na kāmabhogān bahulān nālaṃkārārthasaṃcayān tathaiva bahu manyante yathā ratyām anugraham
english: They do not prize abundant enjoyments, nor heaps of ornaments and wealth, so highly as they prize the favor of the act of love.

sanskrit: antakaḥ śamano mṛtyuḥ pātālaṃ vaḍavāmukham kṣuradhārā viṣaṃ sarpo vahnir ity ekataḥ striyaḥ
english: The Ender, the Subduer, Death, the netherworld, the submarine fire, the razor's edge, poison, the serpent, and flame on the one side—and women on the other.

sanskrit: yataś ca bhūtāni mahānti pañca; yataś ca lokā vihitā vidhātrā yataḥ pumāṃsaḥ pramadāś ca nirmitās; tadaiva doṣāḥ pramadāsu nārada
english: From whatever source the five great elements arose, and the worlds were ordained by the Creator, from that same source men and women were fashioned—and from that very moment, O Nārada, the faults were set in women.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ime vai mānavā loke strīṣu sajjanty abhīkṣṇaśaḥ mohena param āviṣṭā daivādiṣṭena pārthiva striyaś ca puruṣeṣv eva pratyakṣaṃ lokasākṣikam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: These men in the world cleave again and again to women, possessed utterly by a delusion ordained by fate, O king; and women too, plainly and with the world for witness, cleave to men.

sanskrit: atra me saṃśayas tīvro hṛdi saṃparivartate katham āsāṃ narāḥ saṅgaṃ kurvate kurunandana striyo vā teṣu rajyante virajyante 'tha vā punaḥ
english: Herein a keen doubt revolves within my heart: how do men form attachment to these women, O delight of the Kurus, and how do women take pleasure in them, or again grow weary of them?

sanskrit: iti tāḥ puruṣavyāghra kathaṃ śakyāḥ sma rakṣitum pramadāḥ puruṣeṇeha tan me vyākhyātum arhasi
english: Such being so, O tiger among men, how are women able to be guarded by a man in this world? That you ought to explain to me.

sanskrit: etā hi mayamāyābhir vañcayantīha mānavān na cāsāṃ mucyate kaś cit puruṣo hastam āgataḥ gāvo navatṛṇānīva gṛhṇanty eva navān navān
english: For these women beguile men here with the wiles of Maya, and no man once come into their hands escapes them; like cattle to fresh grass, they seize on ever-new men.

sanskrit: śambarasya ca yā māyā yā māyā namucer api baleḥ kumbhīnaseś caiva sarvās tā yoṣito viduḥ
english: All the sorcery that was Śambara's, and the sorcery of Namuci, of Bali, and of Kumbhīnasī—all of it women know.

sanskrit: hasantaṃ prahasanty etā rudantaṃ prarudanti ca apriyaṃ priyavākyaiś ca gṛhṇate kālayogataḥ
english: At one who laughs they laugh, and at one who weeps they weep; and one who is unwelcome to them they take captive with sweet words, as the moment requires.

sanskrit: uśanā veda yac chāstraṃ yac ca veda bṛhaspatiḥ strībuddhyā na viśiṣyete tāḥ sma rakṣyāḥ kathaṃ naraiḥ
english: The science that Uśanas knows, and that which Bṛhaspati knows, are not superior to the cunning of women—how then are they to be guarded by men?

sanskrit: anṛtaṃ satyam ity āhuḥ satyaṃ cāpi tathānṛtam iti yās tāḥ kathaṃ vīra saṃrakṣyāḥ puruṣair iha
english: They call falsehood truth, and likewise truth they call falsehood; how, O hero, are such women to be guarded by men in this world?

sanskrit: strīṇāṃ buddhyupaniṣkarṣād arthaśāstrāṇi śatruhan bṛhaspatiprabhṛtibhir manye sadbhiḥ kṛtāni vai
english: By drawing forth the very cunning of women, O slayer of foes, the treatises on statecraft, I think, were composed by the good—by Bṛhaspati and the rest.

sanskrit: saṃpūjyamānāḥ puruṣair vikurvanti mano nṛṣu apāstāś ca tathā rājan vikurvanti manaḥ striyaḥ
english: When honored by men, women turn their minds away from those men; and when cast off as well, O king, women turn their minds away likewise.

sanskrit: kas tāḥ śakto rakṣituṃ syād iti me saṃśayo mahān tan me brūhi mahābāho kurūṇāṃ vaṃśavardhana
english: Who could be able to guard them?—this is my great doubt. Tell me of it, O mighty-armed one, increaser of the line of the Kurus.

sanskrit: yadi śakyā kuruśreṣṭha rakṣā tāsāṃ kathaṃ cana kartuṃ vā kṛtapūrvā vā tan me vyākhyātum arhasi
english: If their guarding can in any way be accomplished, O best of the Kurus, or has ever been accomplished of old, that you ought to explain to me.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evam etan mahābāho nātra mithyāsti kiṃ cana yathā bravīṣi kauravya nārīṃ prati janādhipa
english: Bhīṣma said: So it is, O mighty-armed one; in this there is nothing false, even as you say concerning woman, O Kaurava, O lord of men.

sanskrit: atra te vartayiṣyāmi itihāsaṃ purātanam yathā rakṣā kṛtā pūrvaṃ vipulena mahātmanā
english: On this I shall relate to you an ancient tale—how of old a guarding was accomplished by the great-souled Vipula.

sanskrit: pramadāś ca yathā sṛṣṭā brahmaṇā bharatarṣabha yadarthaṃ tac ca te tāta pravakṣye vasudhādhipa
english: And how women were created by Brahmā, O bull of the Bhāratas, and to what end—that too I shall declare to you, my son, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: na hi strībhya paraṃ putra pāpīyaḥ kiṃ cid asti vai agnir hi pramadā dīpto māyāś ca mayajā vibho kṣuradhārā viṣaṃ sarpo mṛtyur ity ekataḥ striyaḥ
english: For there is nothing, my son, more given to wickedness than women; a woman is blazing fire, and the wiles born of Maya, O lord; the razor's edge, poison, the serpent, and Death on the one side—and women on the other.

sanskrit: imāḥ prajā mahābāho dhārmikā iti naḥ śrutam svayaṃ gacchanti devatvaṃ tato devān iyād bhayam
english: These creatures, O mighty-armed one—being righteous, so we have heard—were attaining godhood of their own accord; and thereupon fear came upon the gods.

sanskrit: athābhyagacchan devās te pitāmaham ariṃdama nivedya mānasaṃ cāpi tūṣṇīm āsann avāṅmukhāḥ
english: Then those gods came to the Grandsire, O subduer of foes; and having laid bare what was in their minds, they stood silent, their faces downcast.

sanskrit: teṣām antargataṃ jñātvā devānāṃ sa pitāmahaḥ mānavānāṃ pramohārthaṃ kṛtyā nāryo 'sṛjat prabhuḥ
english: Knowing what lay hidden within those gods, the Grandsire, the lord, for the deluding of men, created women as instruments of bewitchment.

sanskrit: pūrvasarge tu kaunteya sādhvyo nārya ihābhavan asādhvyas tu samutpannā kṛtyā sargāt prajāpateḥ
english: In the first creation, O son of Kuntī, women here were virtuous; but the unvirtuous, the instruments of bewitchment, arose from the later creation of Prajāpati.

sanskrit: tābhyaḥ kāmān yathākāmaṃ prādād dhi sa pitāmahaḥ tāḥ kāmalubdhāḥ pramadāḥ prāmathnanta narāṃs tadā
english: To them the Grandsire granted desires according to their wish; and those women, greedy for pleasure, then set to tormenting men.

sanskrit: krodhaṃ kāmasya deveśaḥ sahāyaṃ cāsṛjat prabhuḥ asajjanta prajāḥ sarvāḥ kāmakrodhavaśaṃ gatāḥ
english: The lord of gods created Anger as the helper of Desire; and all creatures, fallen under the sway of desire and anger, grew enthralled.

sanskrit: na ca strīṇāṃ kriyā kā cid iti dharmo vyavasthitaḥ nirindriyā amantrāś ca striyo 'nṛtam iti śrutiḥ
english: And no sacred rite belongs to women—so the law is established; women are without sacred rites and without mantras, untruth itself—so says the śruti.

sanskrit: śayyāsanam alaṃkāram annapānam anāryatām durvāgbhāvaṃ ratiṃ caiva dadau strībhyaḥ prajāpatiḥ
english: Couch and seat, adornment, food and drink, ignobleness, foul-tongued speech, and the pleasure of love—these Prajāpati gave to women.

sanskrit: na tāsāṃ rakṣaṇaṃ kartuṃ śakyaṃ puṃsā kathaṃ cana api viśvakṛtā tāta kutas tu puruṣair iha
english: Their guarding cannot in any way be accomplished by a man—not even by the Maker of All, my son; how much less by mortal men here?

sanskrit: vācā vā vadhabandhair vā kleśair vā vividhais tathā na śakyā rakṣituṃ nāryas tā hi nityam asaṃyatāḥ
english: Neither by word, nor by slaying and bonds, nor by manifold torments can women be guarded; for they are ever unrestrained.

sanskrit: idaṃ tu puruṣavyāghra purastāc chrutavān aham yathā rakṣā kṛtā pūrvaṃ vipulena gurustriyaḥ
english: But this, O tiger among men, I have heard in former times: how of old a guarding was wrought by Vipula over his preceptor's wife.

sanskrit: ṛṣir āsīn mahābhāgo devaśarmeti viśrutaḥ tasya bhāryā rucir nāma rūpeṇāsadṛśī bhuvi
english: There was a seer of great fortune, renowned by the name of Devaśarman; his wife was named Ruci, unmatched in beauty upon the earth.

sanskrit: tasya rūpeṇa saṃmattā devagandharvadānavāḥ viśeṣatas tu rājendra vṛtrahā pākaśāsanaḥ
english: By her beauty were maddened the gods, gandharvas, and dānavas, and most of all, O king of kings, the slayer of Vṛtra, the chastiser of Pāka.

sanskrit: nārīṇāṃ caritajñaś ca devaśarmā mahāmuniḥ yathāśakti yathotsāhaṃ bhāryāṃ tām abhyarakṣata
english: Now Devaśarman, the great sage, knew well the ways of women, and he guarded that wife of his to the utmost of his power and resolve.

sanskrit: puraṃdaraṃ ca jānīte parastrīkāmacāriṇam tasmād yatnena bhāryāyā rakṣaṇaṃ sa cakāra ha
english: And he knew Puraṃdara to be one who lusted after other men's wives; therefore he kept watch over his wife with diligent care.

sanskrit: sa kadā cid ṛṣis tāta yajñaṃ kartumanās tadā bhāryāsaṃrakṣaṇaṃ kāryaṃ kathaṃ syād ity acintayat
english: Once, my son, that seer, minded to perform a sacrifice, fell to pondering how the guarding of his wife might be accomplished.

sanskrit: rakṣāvidhānaṃ manasā sa vicintya mahātapāḥ āhūya dayitaṃ śiṣyaṃ vipulaṃ prāha bhārgavam
english: Having devised in his mind the manner of her guarding, that great ascetic summoned his beloved disciple, Vipula of Bhṛgu's line, and spoke to him.

sanskrit: yajñakāro gamiṣyāmi ruciṃ cemāṃ sureśvaraḥ putra prārthayate nityaṃ tāṃ rakṣasva yathābalam
english: 'I shall go to perform a sacrifice; and this Ruci the lord of the gods forever woos. My son, guard her to the best of your power.'

sanskrit: apramattena te bhāvyaṃ sadā prati puraṃdaram sa hi rūpāṇi kurute vividhāni bhṛgūdvaha
english: 'You must remain ever vigilant against Puraṃdara, for he assumes shapes of many kinds, O scion of Bhṛgu.'

sanskrit: ity ukto vipulas tena tapasvī niyatendriyaḥ sadaivogratapā rājann agnyarkasadṛśadyutiḥ
english: Thus addressed by him, Vipula the ascetic—his senses subdued, ever fierce in penance, O king, radiant like fire and the sun,

sanskrit: dharmajñaḥ satyavādī ca tatheti pratyabhāṣata punaś cedaṃ mahārāja papraccha prathitaṃ gurum
english: knower of dharma and speaker of truth—answered, 'So be it'; and then, O great king, he further questioned his renowned preceptor in these words.
